founders.title: Founder/CEO
founders.founder_bio:
I'm the founder of Silica, a company that designs & manufactures intelligent robotic hardware.

Before Silica, I worked in the product design department at Apple, where I developed novel materials & mfg processes for future products, taking them from the lab to tens of millions of units sold annually. 

Before Apple, I worked as the founding engineer at Artefact, where we made the world's first desktop manufacturing cell that can mold composites.

launches.title: Silica: Actuators for Physical AI
launches.tagline: Sensitive hardware that helps robots feel the world around them
launches.body:
## **TL;DR**

Silica makes the first actuators that can sense force at an affordable price, so that all robots can feel the world around them. Customers have requested more than 60,000 units within a month of launching pre-orders. 

Our Launch Video: <https://youtu.be/KhL5KK1SEH0>

## **Problem**

The robot arms used to train physical AI can't feel anything lighter than a tennis ball. So the data collected on them doesn't accurately record how hard they push. Torque sensors cost several times more than the actuators, so most arms go without them.

## **Solution**

Our actuators integrate sensors into the gearbox, so the joint can feel objects as light as a paperclip. Our tech only adds a little bit (10–15%) to the price of a standard actuator, so the long tail of the industry can have access to physical intelligence. They’re also integrated right into the actuator, so that you don’t have to add a clunky retro-fit to your designs. 

We've designed three sizes to kick off our platform. They drop into today's low-cost training arms with no redesign required. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125282&key=user_uploads/730778/e5fb7b31-3bf4-4499-885b-404a39c3275b)

Our actuators can go into almost anything that moves: factory robots that assemble parts, lab robots that handle samples, and eventually humanoids. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125282&key=user_uploads/730778/a3b5a2f4-e955-4464-aa4c-5476735c108a)

Long term, we want to make embodied AI in its final form.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125282&key=user_uploads/730778/c6a03639-ecc8-4352-9e4c-52dc23896c20)

## **Team**

Before Silica, I worked in the product design department at Apple, where I developed composite materials for new products. Before Apple, I was the first employee at Artefact, where I helped build the first automated, low-power manufacturing cell for a composite manufacturing process called VARTM. 

## **Ask**

* **Any team using actuators**, in arms, humanoids or anything else that moves. Tell us what you use and where it falls short. Pre-orders are open at [silicamachines.com](http://silicamachines.com), and samples ship in February. 
* **Teams collecting data to train robots.** We'd like to hear what torque data would change for you.
* **Engineers who have designed motors, gearboxes or motor controllers.** We're hiring, for both mechanical and electrical/firmware roles.
